newsitem.title: UK: UK's Daily Telegraph retains circulation lead.
newsitem.headline: UK's Daily Telegraph retains circulation lead.

text.p: Britain's Daily Telegraph remained the country's top-selling broadsheet newspaper in April, despite a slight drop in circulation from March, the UK Audit Bureau of Circulation said on Friday.
Circulation of the Daily Telegraph, owned by Canadian publisher Hollinger Inc, edged off 0.26 percent in April to 1,132,931, the Audit Bureau reported.

The Times, part of Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd and arch-rival to the Telegraph, posted a 3.72 percent drop in April circulation to 719,308. But the Times' average daily circulation for the six months ended in April rose 15.44 percent to 772,317 from 669,028 in the comparable, prior-year period.
The Daily Telegraph's average daily circulation for the November to April six months nosed up 0.19 percent to 1,126,479 from 1,041,172 a year earlier.

The Sunday Times continued to dominate the Sunday broadsheet newspaper market, with average daily circulation for the six months up 3.78 percent to 1,338,396. But the Sunday Telegraph's average daily circulation for the six months jumped 33.83 percent to 883,078, the Audit Bureau said.

Circulation of the Independent continued to slide, falling 2.73 percent to 250,551 in April from 257,589 in March. The paper's circulation for the six months ended April 1997 plunged 10.10 percent to 256,161, the Audit Bureau said.
